article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Early Pearl × Early Girl × Super Skunk
Breeder: Mr. Nice Seedbank
THC Content: 17-19%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Tropical fruit, tangerine, grape, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 42–56 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: September
Indoor Yield: 500–550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Beginner-friendly to intermediate

Early Queen was built around a problem that still frustrates outdoor cannabis growers today: excellent marijuana genetics are of little value if autumn rain, cold nights, or mold arrive before the flowers mature. Nevil Schoenmakers and Shantibaba addressed that challenge by combining Early Pearl, Early Girl, and Super Skunk into a three-way hybrid capable of finishing substantially earlier than many traditional varieties. The result has been part of the Mr. Nice genetic library since the early 1990s and remains particularly useful in northern climates, greenhouses, and gardens where the growing season is short. Mr. Nice lists a remarkably quick 42–56-day indoor bloom and September outdoor harvest potential, yet production remains substantial at roughly 500–550 g/m² indoors and around 500 g per plant outdoors.

Speed, however, is only part of the appeal. Shantibaba has described the cultivar as having an unusual terpene profile compared with other strains, and modern grows continue to reveal surprising diversity: tropical fruit, grapes, tangerine, pine, herbs, pepper, sweet Skunk, and even creosote-like tones have appeared among different plants. That combination of early maturation, resilient structure, flavor diversity, and respectable potency gives Early Queen more depth than a simple “fast outdoor weed” label suggests.
Genetics and Lineage

The official family tree is Early Pearl × Early Girl × Super Skunk. Mr. Nice describes the genetic foundation as early Californian blends with a touch of Mexican influence, reflecting the older North American material that sits behind the Early Pearl and Early Girl side of the pedigree. Early Pearl itself belongs to Nevil’s early outdoor breeding work and traces partly to Mexican-influenced Californian genetics selected for rapid flowering, distinctive aroma, and improved performance in humid conditions. Nevil later recalled that Early Pearl material was particularly useful for early flowering and mold resistance—exactly the characteristics needed for northern outdoor cannabis.

Super Skunk contributes a different package: stronger flower structure, resin, pungency, hybrid vigor, and greater production. Together, the parents create considerable phenotype diversity. Some plants display broader, more indica-like leaves and compact structures, while others retain narrower foliage and more obvious sativa expression. Contemporary Mr. Nice grows have documented both forms within the same seed population. That diversity is not a flaw; it reflects a classic breeding approach in which growers can search a population for the balance of earliness, aroma, plant architecture, and effect that best suits their environment.
Effects and Experience

The experience can vary more than it does with a single commercial clone. Well-selected plants have been described as surprisingly potent, with a substantial high that can cut through expectations created by the cultivar’s reputation as an early outdoor variety. One detailed outdoor report characterized the smoke as smooth, strong, and comfortable rather than sharply racy, while noting enough potency to compete favorably with considerably newer dispensary genetics.

Many expressions begin with a relaxed mental lift rather than immediate couch-lock. Attention can become more absorbed, conversation easier, and music or outdoor activities more enjoyable before a steadier physical calm develops. Depending on phenotype, some plants may feel more stimulating while broader-leaf selections can lean heavier. Because no standardized THC percentage exists, consumers should treat each batch independently. Excessive THC can still impair coordination, memory, and judgment or produce anxiety and dizziness, even when the weed feels smooth and easygoing.
Medical Benefits

Early Queen has not been studied in clinical trials as a treatment for any specific condition. Its early breeding history predates much of the modern medical marijuana industry, and assigning therapeutic effects based solely on the strain name would overstate the evidence. Some consumers may prefer its balanced effects when seeking temporary relief from discomfort, tension, poor appetite, or difficulty relaxing, but those experiences cannot establish medical efficacy.

Research on cannabis more generally suggests modest benefits for certain forms of chronic pain, while evidence involving sleep and several other conditions remains less certain. NCCIH also notes that cannabinoid effects depend heavily on the preparation being studied and that adverse effects can include dizziness and sleepiness. Anyone using cannabis alongside medications or for persistent health symptoms should rely on medical guidance and current product testing rather than historical strain reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

A single flavor description does not capture Early Queen particularly well. Shantibaba himself has commented that the cultivar possesses an unusual terpene profile, and grow reports show why. One outdoor selection was described as combining tropical fruit with herbs and an almost mustard-like quality, while another grow documented grapes, tangerines, passion-fruit-like sweetness, pepper, and old Mexican-style creosote notes. More recent plants have shown pine and plum character.

The Super Skunk component supplies enough pungent earth and cannabis funk to keep those brighter notes grounded. Depending on phenotype, the palate may move from sweet fruit into dry herbs and spice or lean more heavily toward pine, Skunk, and earthy resin. No breeder-issued laboratory terpene panel has been published, so assigning permanent percentages of myrcene, limonene, pinene, or another compound would be speculative. In this case, the unusual sensory diversity documented by the breeder and growers is more useful than an invented chemical formula.
Growing Information

Practicality is the reason Early Queen exists. Mr. Nice gives an indoor flowering window of just 42–56 days and recommends the strain to everyone from novice growers to experienced cultivators. Indoor yields are listed at approximately 500–550 g/m², while outdoor plants can reach around 500 g each under favorable conditions. In the Northern Hemisphere, harvest can arrive as early as September, making the cultivar especially attractive where October weather brings persistent rain, falling temperatures, or mold pressure.

Outdoor performance appears to remain one of its strongest qualities. A detailed Ontario grow found vigorous plants with sturdy stems capable of handling severe winds, while many later-finishing marijuana strains in the same garden suffered mold or failed to mature satisfactorily. Plants can become large when given unrestricted root space, so containers should be sized appropriately. Indoors, phenotype variation makes early observation useful: squat selections can work well in compact canopies, while more sativa-expressive plants may benefit from training to maintain even height.

The short flowering cycle does not eliminate the need for airflow or environmental control. Dense Skunk-influenced flowers can still hold moisture, particularly during cool autumn nights. Good spacing, adequate air circulation, and monitoring the interior of larger buds remain important. Because aroma is one of the cultivar’s strongest attractions, slower drying and careful curing are preferable to high-temperature drying that can erase the delicate tropical, citrus, and herbal portion of the profile.
FAQ
What strain is Early Queen?

Early Queen is a classic three-way cannabis hybrid from Mr. Nice Seedbank combining Early Pearl × Early Girl × Super Skunk. It was designed for fast indoor flowering and reliable outdoor maturation in short-season climates.
Who bred Early Queen?
The cultivar is credited to Nevil Schoenmakers and Shantibaba and is maintained within the Mr. Nice/Shantibaba Seeds old-school genetic collection.
How long does Early Queen take to flower?

Mr. Nice lists approximately 42–56 days indoors, or six to eight weeks. Outdoor plants can finish as early as September in the Northern Hemisphere and around March to April in the Southern Hemisphere.
What does Early Queen taste like?

Flavor varies considerably between phenotypes. Documented examples include tropical fruit, grapes, tangerine, herbs, pepper, pine, plum, sweet Skunk, and unusual creosote-like or spicy notes. Shantibaba has specifically described the strain’s terpene profile as unusually distinctive.
Is Early Queen good for outdoor growing?

Outdoor performance is one of its principal strengths. The early September harvest potential, strong production, and history of selection for short seasons make it particularly useful in cooler northern climates and greenhouses where late autumn weather limits longer-flowering marijuana varieties.
Final Thoughts on Early Queen

Early Queen is a cultivar whose greatest strengths become obvious only when its breeding purpose is understood. Nevil and Shantibaba were not trying to make the longest-flowering, most exotic indoor showpiece. They combined Early Pearl, Early Girl, and Super Skunk to create weed that could mature quickly, produce worthwhile yields, tolerate challenging outdoor seasons, and still provide enough aroma and potency to satisfy experienced consumers.

The breeder specifications remain impressive decades later: six to eight weeks indoors, roughly 500–550 g/m², around 500 g per plant outdoors, and September harvest potential across much of the Northern Hemisphere. Just as importantly, the strain has retained considerable sensory diversity. Tropical fruit, citrus, herbs, spice, pine, plum, Skunk, and stranger old-school aromas can all appear depending on the plant selected.

For growers dealing with short summers, autumn humidity, or a need for rapid indoor turnover, that combination still has practical value. Early Queen is not simply an old fast-finishing strain kept alive for nostalgia. It remains a useful example of purposeful cannabis breeding: early Californian and Mexican-influenced genetics reinforced with Super Skunk to create a resilient, productive, flavorful cultivar capable of finishing before the weather does.
